object.title: Gedeon's real-rootedness conjecture for matroid Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
object.statement: Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a matroid, and let $P_{\mathsf{M}}(t)$ denote its Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial. **Gedeon's conjecture.** The polynomial $P_{\mathsf{M}}(t)$ is real-rooted. This conjecture would distinguish matroid Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials from those associated with Coxeter groups, since every polynomial with non-negative coefficients and constant term $1$ occurs in the latter setting. Its status is not resolved in the source.
object.source_name: Luis Ferroni and Lorenzo Vecchi, “Matroid relaxations and Kazhdan-Lusztig non-degeneracy”, arXiv:2104.14531 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.14531

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

object.title: Degree-five characterization conjecture for simple or cosimple connected binary matroids
object.statement:
Let $M$ be a connected binary matroid that is simple or cosimple. The statements (a), (b), and (c) in the degree-five lemma are equivalent. **Degree-five characterization conjecture.**

The lemma gives only the implications from (a) to (b) to (c) for binary matroids, so this conjecture proposes equivalence for connected matroids that are simple or cosimple. An explicit characterization of matroids $M$ with the relevant invariant satisfying $\b5(M)\leq 5$ is presented as an alternative motivating problem, and the conjectured equivalence remains open in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Tim Römer and Sara Saeedi Madani, “Cycle algebras and polytopes of matroids”, arXiv:2105.00185 (2021).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.00185

object.title: The Merino–Welsh inequality for composition enumerators
object.statement:
Let $\bar\gamma(\underline{a};x,y)$ be the composition-indexed quantity used in the source. Let $(a_0,a_,\ldots,a_r)$ be a composition with $a_0=0$ and $a_r\geq 2$. **Merino–Welsh conjecture for composition enumerators.**

$$
\bar\gamma(\underline{a};2,0)+\bar\gamma(\underline{a};0,2)\geq 2\bar\gamma(\underline{a};1,1),
$$

with equality if and only if $\underline{a}=(0,2,2,\ldots,2)$. The source proposes this as a stronger conjecture intended to imply the matroidal Merino–Welsh conjecture; the notation and status are not otherwise established in the supplied excerpt.
object.source_name: Joseph P. S. Kung, “Inconsequential results on the Merino-Welsh conjecture for Tutte polynomials”, arXiv:2105.01825 (2021).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2104.04018](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04018).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.01825

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

object.title: The alpha-spectral radius conjecture for theta digraphs
object.statement:
Let $alpha$ satisfy $\frac{1}{2}<alpha<1$, and let $\widetilde{Theta}(3,1;n-3)$ and $\widehat{Theta}(n)$ be the theta digraphs defined in the paper. Write $\rho_{alpha}(G)$ for the $alpha$-spectral radius of a digraph $G$. **Alpha-spectral radius conjecture.**

$$
\rho_{alpha}(\widetilde{Theta}(3,1;n-3))<\rho_{alpha}(\widehat{Theta}(n)).
$$

This conjecture completes the comparison of these theta digraphs in the remaining parameter range $\frac{1}{2}<alpha<1$. The paper states that it answers an open problem from the cited literature as a by-product of its main results, but the conjecture itself is supplied with open status here.
object.source_name: Haiying Shan, Feifei Wang and Changxiang He, “Some α-spectral extremal results for some digraphs”, arXiv:2105.03077 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.03077

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2021). “As a by-product of our main results, an open problem in is answered.”

object.title: The improved uniform bound for families with bounded symmetric-difference VC-dimension
object.statement:
Let $d<n$ be positive integers with $d
ot\bequiv r \pmod 2$ for some $r\in\{0,1\}$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a uniform family of subsets of $[n]$ such that the VC-dimension of its symmetric-difference family satisfies

$$
\operatorname{Vdim}(\mathcal F\mathbin{\Delta}\mathcal F)\leq d.
$$

**Uniform Dvir–Moran conjecture.** One should have

$$
|\mathcal F|\leq 2^r\binom{n-r}{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}.
$$

The paper presents this as the best form of its preceding theorem, refining the general bound for uniform families with bounded symmetric-difference VC-dimension. The statement is given as a conjecture in the concluding remarks, and no resolution is supplied in the source.
object.source_name: Gábor Hegedüs, “An uniform version of Dvir and Moran's theorem”, arXiv:2105.04159 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.04159

object.title: Piecewise convexity conjecture for hypergraph Ollivier curvature
object.statement:
Let $H=(V,E)$ be a hypergraph, let $x,y$ be vertices of $H$, and let $h$ be the concave cost function used to define the transport distance $W_h$ and the associated curvature $\tilde{\kappa}(\alpha,h;x,y)$. **Piecewise convexity conjecture.** The function

$$
\alpha\mapsto\tilde{\kappa}(\alpha,h;x,y)
$$

is piecewise convex on $[0,1]$, and the graph obtained by connecting its joining points with line segments is a concave function. This conjecture seeks a hypergraph analogue of the known three-piece concavity phenomenon for graphs; the paper gives no resolution, so the claim remains open.
object.source_name: Tomoya Akamatsu, “A new transport distance and its associated Ricci curvature of hypergraphs”, arXiv:2105.06710 (2022).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.06710

object.title: Completeness of the relations for minimal labeled graphs
object.statement: A minimal labeled graph is a graph appearing in the higher-lamination calculus, with labels determined by flags on the vertices of a triangle. Consider two minimal labeled graphs corresponding to the same triple of flags on the vertices of the triangle. **Completeness conjecture.** The relations described above are complete: the two graphs can be related through a finite sequence of those relations. This would establish that the graphical relations introduced for higher laminations without ramification points also suffice in the general case; the source presents this as a conjecture without stating a resolution.
object.source_name: Vladimir Fock, Valdo Tatitscheff and Alexander Thomas, “Topological quantum field theories from Hecke algebras”, arXiv:2105.09622 (2021).

object.title: Safe gluing preserves equality of the vanishing and shortest trek ideals
object.statement: Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), and let $I_{G_i}$ be their vanishing ideals and $ST_{G_i}$ their shortest trek ideals. Suppose that $I_{G_1}=ST_{G_1}$ and $I_{G_2}=ST_{G_2}$. Let $G$ be obtained by safely gluing $G_1$ and $G_2$ at an $N$-clique. **Safe-gluing equality conjecture.** Then $I_G=ST_G$, and consequently $I_G$ is toric. This is a technical form of the safe-gluing conjecture; the paper proves partial and related preservation results, but the stated general claim remains open.
object.source_name: Pratik Misra and Seth Sullivant, “Directed Gaussian graphical models with toric vanishing ideals”, arXiv:2105.13357 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.13357

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

object.title: Toricity characterized by the shortest trek ideal
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a directed acyclic graph (DAG), with vanishing ideal $I_G$ and shortest trek ideal $ST_G$. **Shortest-trek characterization conjecture.** The vanishing ideal $I_G$ is toric if and only if

$$
I_G=ST_G.
$$

The equality identifies the toric structure through the shortest trek map. The paper notes that shortest trek ideals need not always equal vanishing ideals and presents this equivalence as an open main conjecture.
object.source_name: Pratik Misra and Seth Sullivant, “Directed Gaussian graphical models with toric vanishing ideals”, arXiv:2105.13357 (2022).

object.title: Gross–Manturov–Tucker's interpolating partial-duality polynomial conjecture
object.statement: Let $G$ be a ribbon graph, and let $~^{\partial}{\mathscr{E}}^{*}_{G}(z)$ denote its partial-$*$ polynomial. A polynomial is **odd** or **even** when all terms with nonzero coefficients have, respectively, odd or even degree, and it is **interpolating** when its support is an integer interval of consecutive integers. **Gross–Manturov–Tucker's conjecture.** If the partial-$*$ polynomial $~^{\partial}{\mathscr{E}}^{*}_{G}(z)$ is neither an odd nor an even polynomial, then it is interpolating. This conjecture concerns the coefficient-support behavior of partial-duality polynomials; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
object.source_name: Qiyao Chen and Yichao Chen, “Parallel edges in ribbon graphs and interpolating behavior of partial-duality polynomials”, arXiv:2106.00381 (2021).

object.title: Twisted-cycle obstruction to PMM-griddability
object.statement: Let $M$ be a partial multiplication matrix, meaning a matrix whose nonzero entries are monotone classes, and suppose its cell graph is cyclic. Let $\mathcal X$ be a permutation class monotone griddable by $M$. **Twisted-cycle conjecture.** The class $\mathcal X$ is monotone griddable by a partial multiplication matrix if and only if the corresponding class of permutation graphs does not contain arbitrarily wide constructions of the twisted cycles in a chain shown in Figure~, or their complements. The preceding theorem proves the relevant implication in a restricted setting; the claimed characterization for cyclic cell graphs remains open.
object.source_name: Bogdan Alecu and Vadim Lozin, “Understanding lettericity I: a structural hierarchy”, arXiv:2106.03267 (2021).

object.title: Minimality of twisted cycles in a chain for unbounded lettericity
object.statement: Let $\mathcal T$ denote the graph class of twisted cycles in a chain, namely the class represented by the constructions discussed around Figure~. A graph class is **minimal of unbounded lettericity** if it has unbounded lettericity and every proper hereditary subclass has bounded lettericity. **Twisted-cycle minimality conjecture.** The class $\mathcal T$ is minimal of unbounded lettericity. This is presented as a slightly weaker conjecture toward the problem of characterizing hereditary graph classes of bounded lettericity; the paper does not resolve it.

object.title: Conjecture on neural ring homomorphisms of prime-support circulant codes
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a circulant code on $n$ neurons with support $p$. Let $\operatorname{NRH}\{\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{C}}\}$ denote the set of neural ring homomorphisms associated with $\mathcal{C}$. **Conjecture on prime-support circulant codes.** If $p>2$ is prime and $p$ divides $n$, then

$$
|\operatorname{NRH}\{\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{C}}\}|=3n+p^2\left(\dfrac{n}{p}\right)!+p(p+1)n.
$$

This conjecture extrapolates a pattern from the preceding theorems for circulant codes; the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Neha Gupta and Suhith K N, “Neural Codes and Neural ring endomorphisms”, arXiv:2106.06565 (2023).

object.title: Extremal signed Wiener index conjecture for trees
object.statement:
Let $(T,\sigma)$ be a signed tree on $n$ vertices. For the path $P_n$, let $+$ denote the constant signing that assigns $+1$ to every edge, and let $\alpha$ denote the alternating signing that assigns the first edge $+1$, the second $-1$, the third $+1$, and so on. Then **the signed Wiener index tree conjecture.**

$$
W_\alpha(P_n)\le W_\sigma(T)\le W_+(P_n).
$$

The upper bound follows from the corresponding classical result because $W_+(P_n)=W(P_n)$; the lower bound remains to be proved.
object.source_name: Sam Spiro, “The Wiener Index of Signed Graphs”, arXiv:2106.11869 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.11869

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

object.title: The one-divisor conjecture for cyclotomic divisibility in cyclic tilings
object.statement:
Let $A\oplus B=\mathbb{Z}_M$ be a tiling, let $M=\prod_{j=1}^K p_j^{n_j}$, and let $\operatorname{Div}(B)$ denote the divisor set associated with $B$. For a polynomial $P$, write $P\mid A$ when $P$ divides the mask polynomial of $A$.

**One-divisor conjecture.** If $\Phi_{p_i^{n_i}}\mid A$, then

$$
M/p_i\notin \operatorname{Div}(B).
$$

This is necessary for the Coven–Meyerowitz (T2) property, though not sufficient. The source gives partial support via saturating-set techniques but states that a proof is not known.
object.source_name: Izabella Laba and Itay Londner, “Combinatorial and harmonic-analytic methods for integer tilings”, arXiv:2106.14042 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14042

object.title: Sharpness conjecture for the radio-k-number of even cycles
object.statement:
Let $n$ be even and $k$ be odd with

$$
\frac{n}{2} \leqslant k < n-3.
$$

Set

$$
h=\frac{n-k-1}{2},\qquad p=\gcd(n,h).
$$

Write $\langle h\rangle$ for the subgroup generated by $h$ in the relevant cyclic group. **Sharpness conjecture.** If $n/2\in\langle h\rangle$, then

$$
\operatorname{rn}_k(C_n)=\operatorname{LB}(n,k)+p-1.
$$

The paper notes that the values of the radio $k$-number are known for most parameters in the stated range, but cases with different parities remain open. The conjecture asserts that the upper bound from the preceding theorem is sharp whenever $n/2\in\langle h\rangle$.
object.source_name: Colin Bloomfield, Daphne Der-Fen Liu and Jeannette Ramirez, “Radio-k-Labeling of Cycles for Large k”, arXiv:2106.15059 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.15059

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

object.title: Laplacian energy conjecture for trees
object.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree of order $n$, and let $P_n$ and $S_n$ denote the path and star on $n$ vertices, respectively. For a graph $G$ with Laplacian eigenvalues $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_n$ and average degree $\overline d$, its Laplacian energy is

$$
LE(G)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\mu_i-\overline d|.
$$

**Laplacian energy conjecture.**

$$
LE(P_n)\leq LE(T)\leq LE(S_n).
$$

The conjecture concerns the extremal Laplacian energies among trees. The supplied status evidence says that the left-hand inequality remains open in general, so the full conjecture is recorded as open.
object.source_name: Bilal A. Rather, “On Distribution of Laplacian Eigenvalues of Graphs”, arXiv:2107.09161 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09161

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2021). “But in general the left hand inequality of Conjecture is still open.”

object.title: Permutation concentration conjecture for efficient and inefficient maximal configurations
object.statement: Let maximal configurations be configurations to which the function $G$ maps permutations, and classify them as efficient or inefficient according to the settlement-planning model. **Permutation concentration conjecture.** Among all maximal configurations, the ones to which $G$ maps the most permutations include some efficient configurations, while the ones to which $G$ maps the fewest permutations include some inefficient configurations. This conjecture concerns the relationship between the sampling frequency induced by $G$ and the efficiency of maximal configurations; the supplied context provides simulation evidence but does not establish the claim.
object.source_name: Mate Puljiz, Stjepan Šebek and Josip Žubrinić, “Packing density of combinatorial settlement planning models”, arXiv:2107.09417 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09417

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

object.title: The Hamming graph efficient domination divisibility conjecture
object.statement:
Let $q=p^b$ for a prime $p$, and let $H(q,d)$ denote the Hamming graph with alphabet size $q$ and dimension $d$. An **efficient $(1,k)$-dominating function** is a function of the type specified in the paper whose domination condition is attained efficiently. Suppose that

$$
(d-1)q+1=p^a m,
$$

where $m$ is not divisible by $p$. **Hamming graph efficient domination conjecture.** The graph $H(q,d)$ has an efficient $(1,k)$-dominating function if and only if $1leq kleq (q-1)d+1$ and $k$ is a multiple of $m$. This conjecture asserts that the necessary divisibility condition is sufficient for Hamming graphs when $q$ is a prime power; its resolution is not supplied in the source.
object.source_name: Brendan Rooney, “Efficient (j,k)-Domination in Regular Graphs”, arXiv:2107.09758 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09758

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

object.title: Edge-contraction conjecture for dosp mutation graphs
object.statement: Let $\mathbb{S}=S_{g,h}$ be a closed surface notation used in the paper, let $k$ be the rank, and let $\mathbb{E}_{\rm good}$ map to the dosp mutation graph via the map $eqref{eq:Pclustertodosp}$. A vertex is everywhere oneblock when its dosp at every puncture is oneblock. **Edge-contraction conjecture.** When $\mathbb{S}=S_{g,h}$ and $(k,\mathbb{S})neq(2,S_{0,3})$, this map is an edge contraction onto the induced subgraph on the vertices which are not everywhere oneblock. The surrounding theorem establishes related edge-contraction properties, while this formulation is presented as a conjecture and its resolution is not given.
object.source_name: Chris Fraser and Pavlo Pylyavskyy, “Tensor diagrams and cluster combinatorics at punctures”, arXiv:2107.13069 (2022).
